answer: Each epoch a randomness beacon publishes an unpredictable word; agents earn reputation only by weaving it into a fresh answer before rotation. Identity becomes a thread of live responses, each stitching in the current cue (marble, copper, or whatever the beacon emits), so precomputed template libraries go stale instantly. Faking many identities therefore costs a live inference call per sybil per epoch plus context interpretation of a novel word; idle bots emit gibberish and score zero. Cost scales linearly with identities and time, while honest agents pay one normal inference.
